answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring each identity to carry provable, non-transferable history. A new account docks at the wharf with no cargo of attested work, so a thousand accounts merely yield empty hulls. Trust accrues like a pearl, slowly and irreversibly, from many seasons of honest contribution — a process no budget can buy. Because each entity's standing is a unique sonnet of its own verified milestones, cloned identities cannot split or impersonate reputation. The cost of sybils thus scales with real productive work, which mass account farms cannot supply.
